payload.name: access_method
payload.title: ONGA Access Method Record
payload.description: Description of an access method that can be used to fetch a data file, copied from the GA4GH DRS AccessMethod model. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/access-method). Port notes: the enum `AccessMethods` is renamed `AccessProtocol` and the slot `access_method` is renamed `access_protocol` (killing the class/enum one-letter near-clash), and the slot's range is the enum, not the class (adopting the fga-qg add-external-standard-annotations branch's bug fix).

payload.name: access_url
payload.title: ONGA Access URL Record
payload.description: The URL and associated HTTP headers to access a data file, copied from the GA4GH DRS AccessURL model. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/access-url).

payload.name: analysis
payload.title: ONGA Analysis Record
payload.description: The computational processing applied to data from a sequencing experiment or another analysis. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/analysis).

payload.name: checksum
payload.title: ONGA Checksum Record
payload.description: A checksum of a data file, copied from the GA4GH DRS Checksum model. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/checksum).

payload.name: contact
payload.title: ONGA Contact Record
payload.description: Contact information for a person or an organisation. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/contact).

payload.name: deposit
payload.title: ONGA Deposit Record
payload.description: A public deposit of a document containing metadata about a set of genomic annotation files. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/deposit).

payload.name: derivation
payload.title: ONGA Derivation Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary recording the epistemic origin of a file's values: whether they were empirically observed (measured from experimental sequencing data) or computationally predicted (generated by a statistical/computational model rather than directly measured). `Derivation` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set) and a provenance facet — it records how the values were obtained (measured vs. modeled), not what the values mean. It factors the measured-vs-model qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType / FeatureType terms (e.g. "observed signal profile" / "predicted signal profile", "predicted transcription start sites") so that derivation becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `derivation` slot of the `TrackProvenance` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value. An absent value means the derivation is unspecified (NOT a default of observed): the generic `signal profile` term carries no derivation value.

The vocabulary is deliberately two-valued. `control` is EXCLUDED: in the source terms "control" denotes unrelated things — an experimental role (control vs. treatment) or a normalization reference (control-normalized) — not the measured-vs-model axis this facet captures. Control-related terms therefore stay as distinct output_type / feature_type values and are not decomposed onto this facet.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the measured-vs-model axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses, here homed on the provenance schema as a processing/derivation operation.

payload.name: document
payload.title: ONGA Document Record
payload.description: Self-description of a harmonised metadata document — identifiers, deposit versioning, sources, and the ontology versions its Term values resolve against. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/document).

payload.name: donor
payload.title: ONGA Donor Record
payload.description: The donor or complete organism from which a sample was taken. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/donor). Port note: the FGA-WG slot `sex` is renamed `donor_sex` — it records the biological sex of the SAMPLE's donor, which must never be confused with `ReferenceGenome.build_sex` (the sex of the reference assembly build).

payload.name: experiment
payload.title: ONGA Experiment Record
payload.description: A sequencing experiment carried out within a study, based on biological samples, providing data files as output. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/experiment).

payload.name: file
payload.title: ONGA File Record
payload.description: General information about a data file, largely copied from the GA4GH DRS DrsObject model. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/file). Port notes: the FGA-WG `data_content` slot and its ~270-value `OutputType` enum are superseded by ONGA's DataType / FeatureType vocabularies plus facets (the content classification lives in `track_interpretation` on GenomicAnnotationFile; the lossless crosswalk is `mappings/facet_decomposition.tsv`); `file_type` is demoted to optional and cross-mapped to `TrackFormat.file_format`; required-slot demotions follow the ONGA required-slot policy.

payload.name: file_collection
payload.title: ONGA File Collection Record
payload.description: A collection of files according to some selection criteria. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/file-collection).

payload.name: file_content
payload.title: ONGA File Content Vocabulary
payload.description:
ONGA (Ontology for Genomic Annotations) provides controlled vocabularies 
for describing genomic data files. It defines two complementary vocabularies:

- DataType: Computational output types (HOW data was produced)
- FeatureType: Biological feature types (WHAT biology it represents)

A file's DataType describes its computational origin (e.g., "peaks" from a peak caller).
A file's FeatureType describes what biological phenomenon it captures (e.g., "TF binding sites").
The same DataType can represent different FeatureTypes depending on the experiment.
Both vocabularies are **set-denoting**: a DataType or FeatureType term names a file or track whose rows are instances of some element type, not the element itself. Where every row instantiates one Sequence Ontology class, that class is recorded as the term's `element_type` annotation. ONGA is a user of SO, never a substitute for it.

payload.name: filter_status
payload.title: ONGA Filter Status Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary distinguishing the quality-control filtering status of the data a file represents: data retained after QC filtering versus raw data before filtering. `FilterStatus` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set). Unlike read-multiplicity, the filtering axis is NOT read-specific: it applies across output types (reads, alignments, peaks, variants, quantifications, count matrices). It factors the filtered/unfiltered qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "filtered peaks", "unfiltered alignments", "unfiltered sparse gene count matrix") so that QC filtering becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `filter_status` slot of the `TrackInterpretation` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the filtering-status axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses.

payload.name: format
payload.title: ONGA Format Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary of common file formats for genomic annotation tracks. `Format` is a Layer-1 ONGA vocabulary (a closed value set): each permissible value names a track file format, referencing the EDAM ontology (Sequence-annotation-track formats) via `exact_mappings` where a corresponding term exists. It is referenced by the `file_format` slot of the `TrackFormat` descriptor schema.

Ported from / aligned with FGA-WG issue #1 (data formats): https://github.com/fairtracks/fga-wg (issue #1). The FGA #1 discussion distinguishes a format (e.g. narrowPeak) from a column standard (e.g. BED6+3); this vocabulary captures the format axis.

payload.name: genomic_annotation_file
payload.title: ONGA Genomic Annotation File Record
payload.description: The record class for a genomic annotation / track file: a File that composes the five ONGA Layer-2 descriptor schemas (ReferenceGenome, TrackFormat, TrackInterpretation, TrackProvenance, TrackGeometry) into a validatable record. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/genomic-annotation-file). Port notes: the FGA-WG slot `genome_assembly` is renamed `reference_genome` (range: the ReferenceGenome descriptor, which absorbed GenomeAssembly); `sequence_features` (an open Term list) is superseded by the closed FeatureType vocabulary reached via `track_interpretation.feature_type`, whose terms carry `element_type` SO annotations.

payload.name: haplotype_resolution
payload.title: ONGA Haplotype Resolution Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary of haplotype resolution. `HaplotypeResolution` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set) and a CONTENT facet — the second intrinsic-content facet after strand — answering *what the values represent* with respect to allele/haplotype phasing, not an operation applied to the data. It is asserted via the `haplotype_resolution` slot of the `TrackInterpretation` descriptor schema (alongside `strand`), factoring the resolution qualifier out of compound ENCODE / DataType / FeatureType terms (e.g. "haplotype-specific contact matrix", "phased variant calls") rather than baking it into the interpretation value. Absent means haplotype-collapsed / not phase-resolved.

Scope — three deliberately EXCLUDED axes. (1) The parental-origin axis (maternal / paternal) is NOT a value here; it is a separate deferred axis (the `maternal/paternal variant calls` and `maternal/paternal haplotype mapping` terms stay atomic). (2) Reference ploidy (diploid, as in `diploid personal genome alignments`) is NOT a value here — it qualifies the reference, not the resolution. (3) The allelic-imbalance sense of "allele-specific" (e.g. `allele-specific variants`, an allelic-imbalance behavior) is a different sense and is NOT a value of this axis.

Following the facet convention for axes lacking a clean ontology term for the resolution sense, the permissible values carry NO `meaning:` CURIEs.

payload.name: input_source
payload.title: ONGA Input Source Record
payload.description: A qualified reference to the source of a data file, sample, or other entity used as input to a process or result. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/input-source). The qualified-relation shape follows the PROV-O Qualification Pattern; that lineage is recorded as machine-readable annotation on the class, not by restructuring.

payload.name: normalization
payload.title: ONGA Normalization Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary distinguishing the scaling normalization applied to a signal: unprocessed (raw), normalized by sequencing depth / library size, or expressed as a percentage of total signal. `Normalization` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set) and a provenance facet — it records the scaling operation applied to produce the values, not what the values mean. It factors the scaling qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "raw signal", "normalized signal", "percentage normalized signal") so that scaling becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `normalization` slot of the `TrackProvenance` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value. An absent value means the normalization is unspecified (NOT raw): the generic `signal` term carries no normalization value.

This vocabulary covers only the scaling axis. It does NOT cover statistic transforms (p-value, fold-change, z-score, enrichment), which change what the values mean and remain distinct `output_type` (DataType) terms, nor smoothing (wavelet, summed-densities), which stays an output_type.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the scaling-normalization axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses, here homed on the provenance schema as a processing operation.

payload.name: onga
payload.title: ONGA - Ontology for Genomic Annotations
payload.description:
ONGA describes genomic annotation files — their content, encoding, provenance, and research context — in four layers. Layer 1 is a set of closed value vocabularies (DataType, FeatureType, Format, the facet vocabularies, and small structural vocabularies such as AccessProtocol and BiospecimenClassification). Layer 2 is a set of five track-descriptor schemas — classes of slots whose ranges draw on the vocabularies: TrackFormat (how a track is encoded, FGA #1), TrackInterpretation (what it represents, FGA #2), TrackProvenance (what was done to the data — processing/derivation operations), TrackGeometry (its structural shape, FGA #3), and ReferenceGenome (the reference assembly it is defined against, including the seqcol digests and reference-build sex). Layer 3 is the record layer: GenomicAnnotationFile — the class that composes the descriptors into a validatable record — plus File and its DRS-shaped components (Checksum, AccessMethod, AccessURL, InputSource, QualityAssessment). Layer 4 is the investigation layer: the experiment / study / analysis / sample / donor / deposit context of the files, ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/) with machine-readable lineage annotations. Imports and inlined ranges point only downward (Layer 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1); a lower layer refers up only by CURIE value.

ONGA terms denote **sets** of genomic elements — a file, a track, a set of rows. Sequence Ontology terms denote **individual element types**. The two are not the same kind of thing and ONGA never asserts equivalence with an SO class. Where every member of an ONGA set is an instance of one SO class, ONGA records that with `onga:has_element_type`. ONGA is a user of SO, not a competitor to it.

payload.name: quality_assessment
payload.title: ONGA Quality Assessment Record
payload.description: Results of a quality assessment applied to a data file (e.g. peak-calling statistics, BUSCO scores, BEDbase BedStats-style QC numbers). Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/quality-assessment).

payload.name: read_multiplicity
payload.title: ONGA Read Multiplicity Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary distinguishing the read mapping-multiplicity subset used to compute a signal or count track: all mapped reads versus uniquely-mapping reads only. `ReadMultiplicity` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set), and is read-specific. It factors the mapping-multiplicity qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "signal of all reads", "sparse gene count matrix of unique reads") so that the read subset becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `read_multiplicity` slot of the `TrackInterpretation` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the mapping-multiplicity axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses.

payload.name: reference_build_sex
payload.title: ONGA Reference Build Sex Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary recording the sex of the reference genome BUILD a track is defined against — i.e. which sex chromosomes the reference assembly contains (a male assembly carries X and Y; a female assembly carries X only). `ReferenceBuildSex` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set) and a property of the REFERENCE assembly, NOT of the biological sample. It factors the male/female qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "male genome reference", "female genome index") so that reference-build sex becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `build_sex` slot of the `ReferenceGenome` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the content value. An absent value means the build sex is unspecified — a sex-neutral / combined assembly.

IMPORTANT: this records the sex of the reference genome BUILD, NOT the biological sample's sex. Sample sex is a biospecimen property and is delegated to PATO (FAIRtracks has no sex field, so it cannot be imported from the FGA-WG).

payload.name: reference_genome
payload.title: ONGA Reference Genome Schema
payload.description:
Descriptor schema for the reference genome a track is defined against. Every genomic annotation is expressed relative to a reference assembly (FGA-issue adjacent), and properties of that assembly — its identifiers and the sex of the build — are a distinct axis from what the track's content IS (TrackInterpretation), how it was processed (TrackProvenance), how it is encoded (TrackFormat), or its structural shape (TrackGeometry).
`ReferenceGenome` is the 5th ONGA descriptor schema. It carries the reference-build sex factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "male genome reference"): the male/female there qualifies the REFERENCE assembly used (which chromosomes it contains), not the biological sample. It also absorbs the FGA-WG GenomeAssembly class (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/genome-assembly): the seqcol digest slots, accessions, and aliases come from there (the GenomeAssembly class name disappears; two classes for one concept was a collision, and ReferenceGenome was already the Layer-2 descriptor).

payload.name: sample
payload.title: ONGA Sample Record
payload.description: A biospecimen/sample used as raw material for lab experiments. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/sample). This class realizes the biospecimen module anticipated by ONGA design principle #5: sample properties (tissue, cell type, phenotype, donor development stage) are delegated to external ontologies (UBERON, CL, CLO, PATO) via Term-valued slots, never baked into the content vocabularies. `organism_tissue` is the anticipated organism_part landing slot recorded in `mappings/scope_delegations.tsv`.

payload.name: strand_orientation
payload.title: ONGA Strand Orientation Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary of strand orientation. `StrandOrientation` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set): each permissible value names the strand a genomic annotation track represents. It factors the strand qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "minus strand signal", "observed signal profile (plus strand)") so that strand becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `strand` slot of the `TrackInterpretation` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the strand axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses. Where a Sequence Ontology (SO) term exists for the strand sense, it is referenced via `exact_mappings` — never via `meaning:`, which would make the ONGA permissible value's IRI *be* the SO class and so relabel, redefine and re-parent a live SO term in the generated OWL. See the ADR "ONGA terms denote sets; SO terms denote elements".

payload.name: study
payload.title: ONGA Study Record
payload.description: A scientific study — a unit of research within which experiments and/or analyses have been carried out. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/study).

payload.name: term
payload.title: ONGA Term Helper
payload.description: Helper entity for representing an ontology term as a data value (a CURIE plus its human-readable label). Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/term).

payload.name: thresholding
payload.title: ONGA Thresholding Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary recording that a retention cut (a thresholding operation) was applied to produce a file, and the basis of that cut. `Thresholding` is a Layer-1 ONGA facet vocabulary (a closed value set) and a provenance facet — it records that some statistical or quality threshold was used to retain a subset of features/elements, and what that threshold was based on, not what the retained data means. It factors the thresholding qualifier out of compound ENCODE `output_type` / DataType terms (e.g. "IDR thresholded peaks", "mapping quality thresholded contact matrix") so that the retention cut becomes an orthogonal facet asserted via the `thresholding` slot of the `TrackProvenance` descriptor schema, rather than being baked into the interpretation value. An absent value means no threshold was applied or the thresholding is unspecified. This axis cross-cuts output kinds — it applies to peaks, contact matrices, and regulatory (element–gene) links alike.

Aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): the thresholding axis is one of the orthogonal facets a compound interpretation term collapses, here homed on the provenance schema as a processing operation.

payload.name: top_level
payload.title: ONGA Top-Level Deposit Document
payload.description: The root container for a harmonised metadata deposit document: inlined lists of files, experiments, analyses, samples, donors, and file collections, plus the self-describing Document. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/top_level). Deliberately NOT marked tree_root: both standalone GenomicAnnotationFile records and TopLevel deposits must validate.

payload.name: track_format
payload.title: ONGA Track Format Schema
payload.description:
Descriptor schema for how a genomic annotation file is encoded on disk: its primary file format and any format-specific column conventions. `TrackFormat` is a Layer-2 descriptor schema (a class of slots) that records the encoding of a single track; its `file_format` slot draws on the Layer-1 `Format` vocabulary (defined in format.yaml), a closed value set of common genomic track formats aligned with the EDAM ontology.

Ported from / aligned with FGA-WG issue #1 (data formats): https://github.com/fairtracks/fga-wg (issue #1). The FGA #1 discussion distinguishes a format (e.g. narrowPeak) from a column standard (e.g. BED6+3); this schema captures that split via `file_format` plus the conditional `bed_core_columns` / `bed_extra_columns` slots.

payload.name: track_geometry
payload.title: ONGA Track Geometry Vocabulary
payload.description:
Controlled vocabulary describing the overall geometric or structural properties of the sequence features in a genomic annotation file when considered as a one-dimensional genome browser track. The properties follow the track type delineations of Gundersen et al. 2011. While conceptually based on visual characteristics, they are also useful to, e.g., select relevant annotation files for non-visual analyses.

Ported from the FGA-WG track geometry schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/track-geometry), based on Gundersen et al. 2011. Port note (divergence from the fga-qg copy): the enum of value primitives is named `ValueType` here (renamed from `DataTypes`, which was one letter away from the ONGA content vocabulary `DataType` — a different thing entirely).

payload.name: track_interpretation
payload.title: ONGA Track Interpretation Schema
payload.description:
Descriptor schema for what the data in a genomic annotation file represents. Interpretation has two distinct halves: an *algorithmic* concept (the process/output the file represents, e.g. "peaks", "signal") and a *biological* concept (the biological entity it represents, e.g. "TF binding site", "enhancer"). These map onto the `DataType` and `FeatureType` vocabularies defined in file_content.yaml, respectively.

Ported from / aligned with FGA-WG issue #2 (data interpretation): https://github.com/fairtracks/fga-wg (issue #2), which explicitly splits interpretation into an algorithmic concept and a biological concept.

payload.name: track_provenance
payload.title: ONGA Track Provenance Schema
payload.description: Descriptor schema for the processing/derivation provenance of a genomic annotation file — the operations applied to the data to produce it (read selection, QC filtering; extensible to normalization, derivation, and bias-correction). Where `TrackInterpretation` records *what the data is / means*, `TrackProvenance` records *what was done to it*. The murky axes that resisted placement in interpretation (read selection, filtering, normalization, observed/predicted, bias-correction) were murky because they describe processing provenance, not content: `output_type` names a result KIND (a noun), while these name OPERATIONS applied.

payload.name: util
payload.title: ONGA Utility Types
payload.description: Utility helper types. Ported from the FGA-WG schema (https://w3id.org/fga-wg/schema/util).
Aligned sequence reads or assembled sequences mapped to a reference.
Genome annotations, transcript models, and feature tracks.
Open chromatin regions and nuclease cleavage data from DNase-seq or ATAC-seq.
Pairwise interaction frequency data from chromosome conformation capture experiments.
Sparse or dense count matrices from single-cell or bulk sequencing experiments.
Guide RNA libraries, perturbation signals, and quantifications from CRISPR screens.
Contribution scores, predicted signals, and outputs from trained genomic deep learning models.
Methylation state measurements at specific sequence contexts (CpG, CHG, CHH).
Statistical or predicted associations between regulatory elements and target genes.
Haplotype assignments and phased mapping data.
Discrete regions of enrichment identified by peak calling algorithms.
Gene, transcript, exon, or protein expression measurements.
Genome assemblies, indices, and reference sequences.
Predicted or validated cis-regulatory elements including enhancers, promoters, and CREs.
Replication timing profiles and relative replication signals.
Epitranscriptomic modification states including m6A, m5C, inosine, pseudouridine, and Nm.
Position weight matrices, motif instances, and sequence signatures.
Quantitative signal values across genomic coordinates including coverage, fold change, and p-values.
Cell-level coordinates, annotations, and clustering results from single-cell experiments.
Three-dimensional structural data and predicted ensembles.
Raw instrument output, adapters, barcodes, and technical artifacts.
SNPs, indels, structural variants, and QTL associations.

Access protocols (i.e. communication protocols) for fetching a data file, following the vocabulary defined in the GA4GH DRS specification (renamed from the FGA-WG enum AccessMethods to avoid the near-clash with the AccessMethod class).
Vocabulary from the ENCODE model describing the general category of biospecimen (see "Properties->classification" in https://www.encodeproject.org/profiles/biosample_type).

Computational output types - the data structure or processing result 
a file contains. Describes HOW data was produced or represented.
Examples: peaks (output of peak caller), signal track, alignments, count matrix.

The epistemic origin of a file's values — empirically observed (measured from experimental data) vs. computationally predicted (generated by a model) — factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType / FeatureType terms. A provenance facet recording how the values were obtained, not what they mean. Absent means unspecified (not a default of observed). `control` is deliberately excluded: it denotes an experimental role or normalization reference, not the measured-vs-model axis.

Biological feature types - the biological entity or concept the data 
represents. Describes WHAT biological phenomenon the features capture.
Examples: enhancers, TF binding sites, methylation states, chromatin loops.

The quality-control filtering status of the data a file represents, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. Applies across output types (reads, alignments, peaks, variants, quantifications, count matrices).
Common file formats for genomic annotation tracks. Where an EDAM term exists for the format, it is referenced via `exact_mappings`.
Haplotype resolution of a genomic annotation track, factored out of the compound ENCODE / DataType / FeatureType terms. Absent means haplotype-collapsed / not phase-resolved.

The scaling normalization applied to a signal, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A provenance facet recording the scaling operation applied to produce the values. Absent means unspecified (not raw). Does not cover statistic transforms (p-value, fold-change, z-score, enrichment) or smoothing, which are distinct output_types.
The read mapping-multiplicity subset used to compute a signal or count track (all mapped reads vs uniquely-mapping reads only), factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms.

The sex of the reference genome build used (which sex chromosomes the assembly contains), factored out of compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample. Absent means unspecified / sex-neutral combined assembly.
Strand orientation of a genomic annotation track, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms.

The retention cut applied to produce a file and the basis of that cut, factored out of the compound ENCODE output_type / DataType terms. A provenance facet recording that a threshold was applied. Absent means no threshold / unspecified. Cross-cuts peaks, contact matrices, and regulatory links.
Types of data values associated with sequence features or edges. (Renamed from the FGA-WG enum DataTypes to avoid the near-clash with the ONGA DataType content vocabulary.)

payload.label: alignments

sssom.comment: Direct match: aligned reads to reference

payload.description: Sequencing reads mapped to positions in a reference genome, typically in BAM/CRAM format with mapping quality scores and alignment coordinates.

payload.label: alignments with modifications

sssom.comment: EDAM lacks modification-aware alignment concept

payload.description: Aligned reads preserving base modification information (e.g., methylation from bisulfite-seq or direct detection) encoded in BAM auxiliary fields.

payload.label: diploid personal genome alignments

sssom.comment: EDAM lacks diploid/personal alignment concept

payload.description: Reads aligned to a diploid personal genome reference including both parental haplotypes, enabling allele-specific analysis.

payload.label: gene alignments
payload.description: Reads or sequences aligned at the gene level.

payload.label: preprocessed alignments

sssom.comment: EDAM lacks preprocessing stage qualifier

payload.description: Alignments after preprocessing: duplicate marking, base quality score recalibration, or indel realignment.

sssom.comment: Close match: sequencing reads
Direct match

payload.description: Raw or minimally processed sequencing reads in FASTQ format, including quality scores and read identifiers.

payload.label: redacted alignments
payload.description: Alignments with sensitive genomic positions masked or removed for privacy protection in controlled-access data sharing.

payload.label: redacted transcriptome alignments
payload.description: Transcriptome-level alignments with sensitive positions redacted.

payload.label: rejected reads

payload.description: Reads that failed quality control filters and were excluded from downstream analysis.

payload.description: Reads aligned to exogenous spike-in control sequences (e.g., ERCC) for normalization and quality assessment.

payload.label: transcriptome alignments

payload.description: Reads aligned to a transcriptome reference (cDNA sequences) rather than the genome.

payload.label: base overlap signal
payload.description: Signal computed from base-level read overlap counts at each genomic position.

payload.label: bias-corrected predicted signal profile
payload.description: Model-predicted signal after correction for sequence-composition bias.

payload.label: control normalized signal
payload.description: Signal normalized against a matched control experiment to remove background and technical artifacts.

payload.label: enrichment
payload.description: Quantitative enrichment score over background, measuring signal above expected noise level.

payload.label: fold change over control
payload.description: Signal expressed as the ratio of experimental signal to input/control, highlighting enrichment over background.

payload.label: signal
payload.description: Quantitative signal track showing per-base or per-bin values across the genome, typically in bigWig format.

payload.label: signal p-value

payload.description: Statistical significance track showing -log10(p-value) of enrichment at each position.

payload.label: summed densities signal
payload.description: Signal computed as the sum of per-base read densities across the region.

payload.label: wavelet-smoothed signal
payload.description: Signal smoothed using wavelet transform to reduce noise while preserving peak structure.

payload.label: bidirectional peaks

sssom.comment: EDAM lacks peak directionality concept

Represents a sequencing experiment that has been carried out within a study, based on biological samples, and providing data files as output. A collection of files, according to some selection criteria. This is the natural future home for the BEDset concept (a curated collection of BED files).

Information about a genomic annotation / track file. GenomicAnnotationFile is a specification of the File entity and inherits all the fields defined in File, in addition to the fields that are specific to GenomicAnnotationFile, as detailed here. This is the class that composes the five ONGA descriptor schemas: the required reference_genome (the coordinate system) plus the recommended track_format, track_interpretation, track_provenance, and track_geometry descriptors.

General object representing the source of data files, samples, or other entities used as input to a process or a result. An input source refering to a single file or sample object will represent that item only, while an input source referring to a container or process may represent a number of disctinct input items. InputSource also contains information about the type of relationship, replication labelling, versioning and retrieval date. The qualified_relation values are typically PROV CURIEs (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy, ...) carried as data-level cross-references.

Information about an ontology used in the metadata: a map from the version-agnostic URL to a versioned URL. Version pinning is real work for deposit documents — the OWL versionIRI mechanism serves the same purpose at the ontology level.

Represents the results of a quality assessment that has been carried out on a data file resulting from an experiment or analysis. This is the natural home for repository QC metrics (e.g. BEDbase BedStats numbers). A typed QC vocabulary may later tighten assessment_method; for now it accepts a free string or a Term.

ONGA descriptor schema for the reference genome a track is defined against (FGA-issue-adjacent: every genomic annotation is relative to a reference assembly). Carries content-derived seqcol digests and human-readable identifiers for the exact assembly, plus the sex of the reference build (factored out of compound terms like "male genome reference"). The build sex is a property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample (that is Donor.donor_sex). Absorbs the FGA-WG GenomeAssembly class.

Information about a biospecimen/sample used as raw material for lab experiments. Sample properties are ontology-delegated via Term-valued slots (UBERON for tissue, CL for cell type, CLO for cell line, PATO for phenotype), per ONGA design principle #5.
A scientific study, i.e. a unit of research, within which experiments and/or analyses have been carried out.

Helper entity to represent an ontology term as a data value. Term instances are DATA-LEVEL cross-references: a CURIE carried inside a record, never a schema-level IRI. Schema-level cross-references use mapping slots (exact_mappings/close_mappings/broad_mappings) per ONGA design principle #7, never `meaning:`.
A document of harmonised metadata for a set of genome annotation files. This is the top-level class to be used as root for a metadata deposit document.
How a genomic annotation file is encoded: its primary file format and, for BED-family formats, the number of standard (core) and extra (custom) columns. Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #1.

Overall geometric properties of the sequence features in the genomic annotation file if considered as an one-dimensional genome browser track, in line with the track type delineations from Gundersen et. al, 2011. While conceptually based on visual characteristics, these properties are also useful to e.g. select relevant annotation files for non-visual analyses.

What the data in a genomic annotation file represents, split into an algorithmic interpretation (output_type, drawing on the DataType vocabulary) and a biological interpretation (feature_type, drawing on the FeatureType vocabulary). Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #2.

The processing/derivation operations applied to the data to produce the file: which read subset it was computed from (read_multiplicity), what QC filtering operation was applied (filter_status), and what scaling normalization was applied (normalization), what retention cut / thresholding was applied (thresholding), and the epistemic origin of the values (derivation: observed vs. predicted). This schema is the planned home for further processing facets as they are decided. Boundary with the Analysis record class (Layer 4): TrackProvenance carries faceted, closed-vocabulary descriptors of what was done to the CONTENT; Analysis is the record of the ACTIVITY itself (workflow, tool, version, inputs). The read mapping-multiplicity subset the data was computed from (all mapped reads vs uniquely-mapping reads only) — the read-selection operation applied. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "signal of all reads"). Absent means unspecified.

The reference genome the annotation is defined against, consequently defining the genomic coordinate system for the annotation. Renamed from the FGA-WG slot genome_assembly; the range is the ONGA ReferenceGenome descriptor schema. Required: a genomic annotation without a coordinate system is not a genomic annotation.
Name of the region in the cloud service provider that the object belongs to.
Document detailing the provenance of the experiment or analysis run which produced the file as one of its outputs. The provenance info should include software versions, parameter settings, etc.
Date of sample collection.
Geographical location where the sample was collected.
Human-readable description of the biospecimen/sample and the sampling process.
External, globally unique identifier for the biospecimen/sample.
Internal identifier for the biospecimen/sample (unique within the metadata deposit).
A human-readable description of the sample, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.
Information about the biospecimens/samples used as raw material for lab experiments.
Protocol detailing the collection and treatment of the biospecimen/sample.

Top-level sequence collection digest according to the GA4GH refget, Sequence Collections standard (v1.0). This a globally unique identifier for the genome assembly, algorithmically derivable from the genome assembly content. Usage is to uniquely identify the exact genome assembly used and allow detailed comparisons across genome assembly variants (say, variants of the GRCh38 assembly).

Content-derived digest that uniquely identifies the ordered coordinate system of the genome assembly. (Coordinate systems with the same sequence names and lengths, but where the sequences are ordered differently, will have different ordered digests.). Usage is the ordered coordinate system digest can be used to uniquely generate a chromSizes file, useful in a number of analysis tools. Definition is the ordered coordinate system digest is defined as the level 1 digest of the name_length_pairs attribute of the sequence collection generated from the genome assembly.

Content-derived digest that uniquely identifies the order-invariant coordinate system of the genome assembly. This digest will be shared across all coordinate systems with the same sequence names and lenghts, regardless of the order of the sequences. Usage is the order-invariant coordinate system digest can be used to uniquely describe the coordinate system of a particular genome browser instance and the annotation files that are compatible with it. Definition is the order-invariant coordinate system digest is defined as the level 1 digest of the sorted_name_length_pairs attribute of the sequence collection generated from the genome assembly.
Set of rules which guides how the sequencing protocol was followed. Change-tracking services such as Protocol.io or GitHub are encouraged instead of dumping free text in this field.
Taxonomical classification of the species of the donor/organism.
The strand orientation the file represents. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "minus strand signal"). Absent means unstranded/unspecified.
Abstract of the study.
External, globally unique identifier for the study (preferably a BioStudies CURIE).
Internal identifier for the study (unique within the metadata deposit). Namespace: "study".
Title of the study.

How the track is encoded on disk: the TrackFormat descriptor (file_format drawing on the Format vocabulary, plus BED column conventions).
Geometric properties of the sequence features in the genomic annotation file if considered as an one-dimensional genome browser track (also relevant for non-visual analyses).
What the track content represents: the TrackInterpretation descriptor (output_type / feature_type drawing on the DataType and FeatureType vocabularies, plus the content facets).
What was done to the data: the TrackProvenance descriptor (processing/derivation facets such as read_multiplicity, filter_status, normalization, thresholding, derivation).
Timestamp of content update in RFC3339, identical to created_time in systems that do not support updates. (This is the update time of the underlying content, not of the JSON object.).
